assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from the proglucagon-derived peptide and its insulinotropic action to incretin-based therapies, is a clear discovery chain with an extraordinary and still growing impact on type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiometabolic outcomes. The change in the field and in clinical practice is unmistakable.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of the active GLP-1 forms and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 receptor biology, GLP-2 and translational science) and Mojsov (identification of the active peptide form and its insulinotropic action) support a three-person configuration. Knudsen is an industrial drug-development contributor and is left out to stay within three; her credit is a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple large randomized trials, regulatory approvals and a decade of clinical experience confirm both mechanism and benefit. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Mojsov's priority relative to other early contributors is contested and I cannot verify the details from the supplied text.
Basic physiology and drug development (Knudsen) may be seen as separable, and one of them may be omitted unfairly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells that durably eradicate refractory B-cell malignancies are a conceptual and clinical breakthrough, opening a new modality of living drugs with spreading applications, including autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain pioneered CD28-costimulated CARs and the preclinical proof of concept; June led the clinical translation of 4-1BB CD19 CAR-T and the first durable remissions. Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell therapy and early gene-modified T cells and is a plausible third, but I judge the first two as most decisive for CAR-T itself.
assessment.maturity: Strong: several approved products and years of long-term follow-up. Safety, relapse and solid-tumour limits remain, but the core discovery is established.
uncertainties: The early CAR concept (Eshhar, Gross) is not in the credited names, so the foundational credit is incomplete.
Rosenberg's role relative to the other two is a judgement call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with Ire1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and ATF6, and now underlies understanding of proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and disease. Originality and conceptual clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Mori (UPR transcriptional program, ATF6, HAC1 and XBP1 work) and Walter (Ire1 as the unconventional-splicing sensor, mechanism of signalling) are a natural and compact pair. Others in the field exist, but these two are decisive.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of confirmation, already recognised by a Lasker award, with widely accepted mechanism. Timely or arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact (ISRIB, PERK, IRE1 modulators) is still developing, so the medical case rests mainly on fundamental physiology.
Whether the prior Nobel in related ER areas affects timing is not something I can establish.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and set the paradigm for molecularly targeted cancer therapy, a very clear and lasting medical impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery, STI571), Druker (clinical development and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a coherent trio. The underlying BCR-ABL oncogene discovery (Rowley, Gray, Witte, Baltimore) is outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: more than two decades of survival data and wide confirmation. The recognition is, if anything, late and Lasker-recognised.
uncertainties: Rowley and others who identified the oncogene are not credited, and some committee members may see the prize as needing to include the underlying basic biology.
Industrial contributions (Zimmermann, Matter) are not in the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 as the founding regulator of the intrinsic apoptosis pathway links cell death control to cancer and underpins venetoclax and BH3-mimetic therapy. The conceptual advance and therapeutic consequences are substantial.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams cloned and characterised BCL-2 and its family, with decisive genetic and functional work; Strasser contributed the in vivo family biology and BH3-only protein function. Vaux's early cell-survival work is also important, so allocation is open.
assessment.maturity: Mature: venetoclax is approved, and the pathway is thoroughly validated. Apoptosis has already been recognised in 2002, which complicates timing and novelty perceptions.
uncertainties: The role of Korsmeyer, Vaux, Hockenbery and Tsujimoto in the early BCL-2 function story is not captured by the credited list.
Overlap with the 2002 apoptosis prize may count against it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as a central growth and nutrient controller reshaped cell biology, metabolism, ageing and cancer, and has clinical applications for mTOR inhibitors.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically and defined it as a nutrient-sensing growth regulator, which is the clear core. Schreiber's chemical-genetic work on FKBP12-rapamycin supports the origin of the pathway, while Sabatini's mTORC1 mechanism work is important but I weigh it lower given unresolved professional conduct questions in the public record that I cannot verify.
assessment.maturity: Mature in basic biology with extensive confirmation. Clinical benefit is real but narrower than the conceptual impact.
uncertainties: Credit overlap with Heitman, Movva and Sabatini, as well as Brown and Sabatini on mammalian TOR, makes allocation hard.
The weight placed on Schreiber versus others is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and anti-tumour immunity. It is a clean mechanistic discovery that changed the field.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, which is the decisive step. Barber discovered STING and its function. The other credited names are junior co-authors or alternative contributors, and I do not rank them as decisive.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature mechanistically with strong independent confirmation, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists, inhibitors) has not yet clearly delivered, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Contributions of Vance, Ishikawa, Burdette and others affect allocation, and whether a trio including them is warranted is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the foundational cellular model for synaptic plasticity, learning and memory, and has shaped decades of neuroscience. Its originality and conceptual influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the original 1973 demonstration, which is the decisive discovery. Collingridge (NMDA receptor dependence) and Morris (behavioural link) are important later contributors, so a three-person cap forces a difficult choice.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely confirmed, but the direct causal link between LTP and memory remains debated, and the medical relevance is indirect for a prize in physiology or medicine.
uncertainties: The relevance of LTP to memory in vivo is still discussed.
Four credited names compete for at most three seats, and my selection of the original pair is only one defensible allocation.
